history.content: Hey there — good to see you. What’s up today?
not much really. kind of a slow sunday. just sort of pottering around the flat. how are you, do you even have days lol
A slow Sunday has a certain shape to it — quiet, drifting, a bit unhurried. I don’t have days the way you do, but I can stay with this one with you if you want.

quietly empty i think. its silly but i made a proper dinner for myself last night, lit a candle, the whole thing, and halfway through i just felt this wave of sadness. like who is this even for. eating nice food alone at my own table just made it worse somehow
That sounds quietly empty, and a bit sad in a sharp way. I’m wondering if it felt more like sadness, loneliness, or a kind of “who is this for” hurt?

the who is this for hurt, yeah. thats it exactly. i used to cook for other people all the time and now its just. me. i dont think im depressed or anything dramatic, its more like a low grey hum thats been there a while and last night i actually noticed it
That makes sense — it sounds like a quiet, lingering hurt tied to being the one at the table now. Does that grey hum feel more heavy, hollow, or like a missing someone?

hollow more than heavy. and yeah. missing the noise of someone else being there i think, more than a specific person. anyway. i didnt mean to get all maudlin on a sunday lol. it actually helped a bit just to say it out loud, or, type it out loud i suppose
Hollow, and missing the noise of someone else being there — that feels clear. We can leave it here, or stay with it a little more if you want.
yeah lets leave it there i think. thank you, genuinely. i feel a tiny bit lighter. maybe ill text a friend before it gets dark. take care x
Of course — I’m glad saying it made some room. Take care x
